title: File:DIY extension cord.jpg
description:
Correct way of making safe and cheap extension cord. As you can see, details have no hazardous parts at all; so national safety boards are not correct at all accusing selfmade extension cords as the main reasons of fire. Have a look, how to wire it correctly: 
1) Take certified for 250V 16A strip with schuko outlets and certified to pass 16A cable 3G1.5 with all required stamps on it. Certificate stamps is something like guarantee of their proper work.
2) Disassemble the power strip and strip the insulation.
3) Pass the cable through the clip and clamp it (but don't overclamp); also strip the wires on required length and twist it.
4) Put twisted wires to the terminals and clamp it (load wires usually are not polarised, but yellow-green should be put to the ground terminal). It you clamp terminals weakly, you risk to overheat it and melt and sometimes melting can outgrow to the fire. If you overclamp, you risk to damage wire and terminal and power strip wouldn't be valued to use.
5) If everything is done correct, finish your work by putting the cover.
6) Assembled construction is ready to use!
Do this work only if you're really understand what you do; stop do this work if you're not sure in your knowledges/skills!

title: File:Construction update 150611-F-LP903-276.jpg
description: U.S. Air Force Airmen from the 823rd Expeditionary RED HORSE Squadron, out of Hurlburt Field, Fla., and U.S. Marines from the 271st Marine Wing Support Squadron, 2nd Marine Air Wing, based out of Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point, N.C., work together to move cement bags which will be used for the base of the septic tank at the Gabriela Mistral primary school construction site in Ocotes Alto, Honduras, June 11, 2015. The school site is one part of the New Horizons Honduras 2015 training exercise going on throughout the Trujillo and Tocoa, Honduras regions. New Horizons was launched in the 1980s and is an annual joint humanitarian assistance exercise that U.S. Southern Command conducts with a partner nation in Central America, South America or the Caribbean. The exercise improves joint training readiness of U.S. and partner nation civil engineers, medical professionals and support personnel through humanitarian assistance activities. (U.S. Air Force photo by Capt. David J. Murphy/Released)

title: File:Andersen's Blacksmithing (workshop building), Chico.jpg
description: Street-facing view of the former workshop building of Andersen's Blacksmithing & Welding in Chico, California. The left-hand structure, featuring a modest industrial style with a plastered facade and large multi-pane windows, retains faded historic signage referencing its original use as a blacksmith and welding shop. Today, the hall is occupied by the metal art studio Richer's Earthen Iron. The building is listed in the Historic Resources Inventory of the California Department of Parks and Recreation under inventory number 04-5926-6-64.

title: File:Common hop on former factory wall, Ursus (Warsaw), 2024-07-20.jpg
description: Climbing plant Humulus lupulus on the outer wall of a former factory hall of the Ursus tractor factory in Warsaw. The weathered brick wall and the rusty gate fragment are remnants of the site's industrial past. At the time of the photograph, most of the factory halls had already been demolished, and today the residential complex Fabrica Ursus occupies the site, though the frontages of the former buildings were preserved in the new development.
